name: Picture Gallery – Frontend Image Uploads, AJAX Photo List
author: videowhisper

sections.description:
Elevate your WordPress site with the Picture Gallery plugin, enabling users to easily upload and manage images through a frontend interface. This powerful plugin supports guest uploads with CAPTCHA, generates thumbnails, and integrates seamlessly into your WordPress Media Library. Whether you’re looking to display image portfolios or sell digital photos, this tool is equipped with AJAX updates for live listing, drag-and-drop uploads, and extensive customization options to meet all your photo gallery needs.

Benefits

  • Compact grid, metadata cards and legacy tiles with locally bundled PhotoSwipe.
  • Frontend image editing: crop, resize, rotate, flip, review and restore original composition.

  • Automatic queued thumbnail size refresh and an administrator batch tool.

  • Frontend & Backend Uploads: Allows both visitors and administrators to upload images conveniently.

  • Advanced Security Features: Includes optional Google reCAPTCHA v3 for spam checks; server-side permissions govern uploads.
  • Dynamic AJAX Photo Lists: Updates the gallery live without page reloads, enhancing user experience.
  • Comprehensive Integration: Adds pictures and thumbnails to the WordPress Media Library for easy management.
  • Customizable Access Controls: Set permissions for uploads and gallery views, ensuring content security.
  • Monetization Opportunities: Integrates with plugins like “MicroPayments/FansPaysite – Creator Subscriptions, Digital Content Monetization” to enable photo sales directly from your gallery.
  • Multi-Device Compatibility: Supports uploads from mobile devices, including direct camera uploads on iOS and Android.
  • Enhanced Engagement: Features like the “Rate Star Review” allow visitors to rate and review images, fostering community interaction.
  • Bulk Upload Capabilities: Simplifies the process of adding large volumes of images, saving time and effort.

Key Features

  • adds picture post type to WordPress site with gallery taxonomy
  • allows upload and import of pictures from frontend and backend
  • guest picture upload with Google reCAPTCHA v3 integration, moderator notification
  • generates thumbnail, generates feature image
  • AJAX display and update of picture list
  • shortcodes for listing pictures, upload form, import form
  • mass picture upload
  • mass picture import (from server)
  • setup user types that can share pictures
  • pending picture / approval for user types that can’t publish directly
  • integrates Rate Star Review – AJAX Reviews for Content, with Star Ratings
  • filter pictures by category, tag, name
  • sort pictures by date, views, rating
  • include pictures and thumbs in Media Library (setting)

Guest Picture Upload

  • special shortcode for guest (visitor) picture upload
  • Google reCAPTCHA v3 integration
  • limit uploads per IP
  • moderator notification by email (custom)
  • custom message for upload success
  • persistent form fields in case of error

Access Control: Membership, Sales

  • define global picture access list (roles, user emails & ids)
  • role galleries: assign pictures as accessible by certain roles
  • exception galleries: free, registered, unpublished
  • show preview and custom message when inaccessible
  • integrates MicroPayments/FansPaysite – Creator Subscriptions, Digital Content Monetization plugin to allow selling items

HTML5 Picture Uploader

  • Drag & Drop
  • AJAX (no Submit, page reload required to upload more pictures)
  • multi picture support
  • status / progress bar for each upload
  • unpredictable secure upload file names
  • fallback to standard upload for older browsers
  • mobile camera upload (iOS6+, Android 3+)
  • backend multi upload menu

Recommended for use with these solutions

  • FansPaysite – Creator Subscriptions, MicroPayments, Digital Content – manage content posts including pictures from frontend
  • Paid VideoChat – integrate pictures in performer profiles
  • Video Share VOD – add pictures in addition to videos
  • Broadcast Live Video – add pictures in addition to live channels

If you find this plugin idea useful or interesting, Leave a Review to help us drive more resources into further development and improvements.

If you need custom development or support, Consult VideoWhisper: professional installation, configuration, troubleshooting, compatible hosting, custom development for new options and features.

Reliable member uploads

Member upload forms keep a request identity for each selected picture. Use Check / resume upload after an interrupted connection, or Retry same file to resend the same request. Reusing a request identity with changed image bytes or form fields returns a conflict. Successful uploads are distinguished from submissions awaiting review.

Unresolved browser receipts store the filename, request identity and form fields in session storage (up to 20 per form); successful receipts are removed. Member self-service recovery requires the same WordPress login session. Administrators can inspect the stored journal and recover it after that session expires, while keeping unfinished pictures pending for review. Private server journals retain request fingerprints and picture relationships to prevent duplicate imports; they are preserved on deactivation and uninstall. After eligible abandoned media is cleaned, a compact replay-blocking receipt remains without the original filename or form fields. Completed receipts do not block an administrator-authorized media purge.

Recovery supports a single processing host with working local file locks. Changes to that host, its temporary lock files or configured media storage require administrator review. Retrying a completed request never recreates a trashed or deleted picture. Guest forms use the browser-bound durable workflow described below. Legacy AJAX/raw integrations retain their compatibility responses and do not acquire the new request protocol automatically.

Administrator upload journals and abandoned media

Picture Gallery > Upload Journals lists at most ten records per page, with owner, processing state, picture relationship, worker availability and retention status. Inspect one journal before recovering or abandoning it. Recovery reuses the original picture, leaves existing completed publication unchanged, and sends unfinished drafts for review. Active editor locks, edited drafts, running workers, changed media, replaced temporary locks and different processing hosts require review; no forced takeover is offered.

Abandonment is an explicit, confirmed administrator action. It permanently removes only an unchanged unpublished upload draft; published and pending pictures are preserved. Media is retained indefinitely by default. Enabling cleanup for an abandoned request starts a fresh seven-day retention period, followed by a separate preview and apply step for at most five journals. Reinstating a hold stops future cleanup. No background deletion runs.

Cleanup requires unchanged files with creation evidence and no remaining references. Shared attachments, active/pending picture dependencies, unproven legacy staging files and ambiguous records are retained. Linked media holds cannot bypass the upload retention deadline. A cleaned request identity remains blocked permanently, including after a lost response, so retrying it cannot recreate deleted content. Files with incomplete creation evidence need manual review.

Support

This is a free open source plugin provided as is. If you need further assistance, troubleshooting, custom development to integrate with your site, Consult VideoWhisper.

Demos

Pictures page on various themes:
* Fans Paysite Demo
* Video Share VOD Demo
* Paid Videochat Demo

My Pictures and legacy uploads

Automatic page setup adds My Pictures alongside Pictures, Upload Pictures and Guest Picture. On existing sites it runs once when an administrator next visits wp-admin with automatic setup enabled; existing pages and content are preserved. The logged-in account menu places My Pictures immediately after Browse Pictures. Sites with automatic setup disabled can create a page containing [videowhisper_pictures author_id=”current”].

The shared list shows the current owner’s published, pending, draft, private and scheduled pictures with status labels, excluding trash. Anonymous visitors must log in. Use a numeric author_id to filter published pictures by author; omit it to browse all published pictures. Existing Paid Membership content-management edit links remain available. Picture-specific editing tools are planned separately. Listing requests are capped at 100 pictures and 1,001 pages, and use allowlisted sort keys. Missing thumbnails display a placeholder instead of starting processing during browsing. Exclude personalized shortcode pages from page/CDN caches; the plugin sends private/no-store headers.

Legacy member integrations can continue POSTing to vwpg_upload with the existing vwpg_upload_nonce security value and owner/gallery/category/tag/description fields (or X-Owner, X-Gallery, X-Category, X-Tag, X-Description raw headers). Accepted transports are file multipart, fileselect/fileselect[] forms (at most 20 files), and raw image bodies with X-Filename. All use the shared validator, EXIF processing, manifest and upload journal. HTML success/error responses and published-picture links are preserved; HTTP errors indicate failure. Tags and descriptions are preserved for multi-file forms too.

For retry safety, send a stable 20–80 character alphanumeric/underscore/hyphen request_id field or X-Request-Id header for one logical upload. Reusing it with changed bytes, filename or metadata returns HTTP 409. Multi-file array requests derive a separate identity as SHA-256(request_id + ‘:’ + array index), so retries must preserve file order. Omit the key only for older clients: each submission then creates a new journal and uncertain retries can still create another picture. Existing vwpg_upload_status POSTs use the same nonce and original request_id for single-file lookup/recovery. Recovery requires the same login session, processing host and original lock; administrator Upload Journals supports review. These member identities do not replace signed guest form grants.

Raw requests are streamed in bounded chunks to exclusive temporary files and cleaned on handled outcomes. An uncatchable worker termination before journaling can leave an unreferenced temporary file for host-level temporary-directory cleanup; the plugin never sweeps arbitrary temporary files. Shared-file checks scan at most 50,000 relevant metadata rows and 5,000 retention records in batches of 64, accepting at most 64 KiB per record. Matching option/content checks also use batches of 64 and a 64 KiB payload cap, with at most 1,000 candidate matches. Any scan overflow/error retains the file. Generic content/custom-field/option reference checks remain conservative and can retain false positives; the limits do not imply a complete indexed catalog or a large-site performance guarantee.

Administrator media diagnostics

Picture Gallery > Media Maintenance includes read-only diagnostics. Backend format flags are reported by the configured WordPress editor classes; they do not prove a complete decode/transform/save on this host. JPEG, PNG and GIF remain the upload allowlist. WebP/AVIF flags do not enable those formats or the planned frontend editor.

Effective image limits come from the same policy as image preflight: decoded pixels/edges, WordPress and raw-upload byte ceilings, and the current request’s conservative memory budget. Frontend requests can have different available memory; native library allocations are estimated. Storage checks only inspect whether the configured directory exists and appears writable, without creating it or establishing file ownership.

Counts describe at most twenty pictures and twenty upload records per cursor batch, not site-wide totals. Unknown/duplicate/oversized metadata is reported for review; unfinished uploads can be active or interrupted. Separate picture and upload cursors advance through later batches. No files, image jobs, manifests, locks or journal writes are created by diagnostics. Use the separate existing nonce-protected maintenance/recovery actions after inspection. Access requires administrator manage_options permission; submitted descriptions, email/IP, filenames, paths and worker credentials are excluded from the diagnostic summary.

Can I build a media reference index?

Administrators can use Media Maintenance to build the next 50 metadata and 20 journal/retention option records and prune the next 50 stale hints. The optional index is local to each site and is never created by browsing or activation. Verified hits can avoid broad scans; misses still use conservative scans. It does not establish file ownership, authorize deletion or remove any images.

How do I select grid, cards and PhotoSwipe?

In Picture Gallery settings, open Display and choose Responsive grid or Picture cards and the picture click action. Existing installations keep Legacy until you opt in; fresh defaults use grid and PhotoSwipe. Shortcodes can override these choices:

[videowhisper_pictures layout="grid" viewer="photoswipe" columns="3" perpage="12"]
[videowhisper_pictures layout="cards" viewer="photoswipe" author_id="current" show_caption="1"]

Modern galleries render images and pagination on the server, including without JavaScript. Search, tags, categories and date/view sorting enhance without replacing working images on errors. PhotoSwipe loads locally on first interaction, offers keyboard navigation/zoom/close and browses only the current authorized page. A separate picture details link remains available. Viewer failures preserve ordinary links. There is no periodic background gallery polling in these layouts.

The viewer checks access again when opened. Gallery role/free/registered/unpublished rules, object visibility, VideoWhisper membership roles, active micropayment purchases and paid-through author subscriptions apply before image serialization. Unknown paid states, WooCommerce and myCRED access fail closed unless a read-only entitlement integration confirms them. Public image URLs may still be directly accessible: this feature does not provide protected file storage. Physical files must be locally readable under approved upload/content roots. Very large or animated display images use an existing thumbnail; viewing never regenerates media. Frontend crop/resize/rotate/flip tools are included; masonry and justified layouts remain planned.

Bundled PhotoSwipe 5.4.4 is MIT licensed. Readable source, license and reproducible artifact instructions are included in scripts/photoswipe/readme.txt. No viewing assets are fetched from a CDN.

Existing pictures after an update

No full-library scan runs during activation or upgrade. Picture Gallery imports intact legacy media relationships on demand, preserving picture IDs, URLs, titles, authors, galleries, visibility and original files. Listings and views queue up to three new jobs per request; WP-Cron inventories at most three pictures per worker request without decoding images. Frontend image editing uses the same importer immediately, without waiting for cron. Dashboard lists and both classic/block edit screens also queue preparation automatically.

Ready records are reused. Each automatic inventory is limited to 64 MiB of distinct media files and uses the shared picture lock. Missing, changed, ambiguous, unsupported or unproven historical media stays preserved for review; no ownership is inferred from its location. Failed background imports pause for an hour unless legacy paths/size/mtime change. Opening the authorized frontend editor retries immediately. Disabled WP-Cron can delay background preparation; explicit Media Maintenance inventory remains available. Existing edit generations and unknown manifest versions are never replaced by automatic import.
sections.faq:
What happens to media when a picture is deleted?

Media is retained by default, including after permanent picture deletion, plugin deactivation or uninstall. Picture Gallery > Media Maintenance provides explicit inventory/backfill previews and an opt-in policy for future deletions. Purge waits at least 24 hours and requires a separate cleanup batch. Shared, changed, ambiguous and legacy files without creation provenance are preserved. Backfill does not move or regenerate images. No automatic background purge runs. On multisite, physical gallery purge and abandoned-file cleanup remain disabled; site-local reference scans cannot establish cross-site file ownership.

  • Q: How much does this plugin cost?
    A: This plugin is FREE.

  • Q: Does upload work on mobiles?
    A: Uploading pictures works on latest mobiles. In example on iOS6+ user will be prompted to take picture or select on from camera roll when pressing Choose Files button.

  • Q: How can I add pictures to my site?
    A: Go to VideoWhisper / Picture Gallery / Settings from top admin menu and click Save. This will add the main feature pages to your site and menu. You can disable Setup Pages and manually add the shortcodes as described in Documentation page.= Where do I report security bugs found in this plugin? =

Please report security bugs found in the source code of the Picture Gallery plugin through the Patchstack Vulnerability Disclosure  Program. The Patchstack team will assist you with verification, CVE assignment, and notify the developers of this plugin.

Guest form validation and privacy

Each guest form has its own controls and nonce. Shortcode owner, gallery, category, tag, description and email settings are authoritative; submitted hidden fields cannot override them. Errors preserve valid text fields and ask the visitor to select the picture again. The ordinary HTML form works without JavaScript when reCAPTCHA is disabled. All guest submissions remain pending, including submissions from a logged-in administrator.

The default attempt limit is 20 per connection per hour, including failed form and verification attempts. It uses the web server connection address, ignores forwarded browser headers, and stores only a keyed address hash, count and expiry in a non-autoloaded counter. Counters expire after one hour; subsequent guest attempts with the attempt limit enabled remove up to twenty expired counters. Expired records can remain stored until that later cleanup. Set Guest Upload Attempts per Hour to 0 to disable this tracking. The separate Limit Uploads per IP setting counts existing guest pictures, including pending, draft and trashed items; uploader email and IP metadata remain with those pictures. Shared connections share limits. Configure trusted client addresses at the web server when using a reverse proxy.

Google reCAPTCHA v3 is optional and loads only on guest form pages after an administrator configures a site key. Google’s browser script receives visitor/browser information and issues a token for action vwpg_guest_upload; submitting the form sends that token and the configured secret from the server to Google’s verification endpoint with an eight-second timeout. Missing, failed, low-score, wrong-action, wrong-host or malformed verification responses block intake. See reCAPTCHA, Google Privacy Policy and Google Terms. Disable the site key to remove this integration. No uploader email, description or image bytes are sent by the plugin’s verification request.

Durable guest uploads and browser receipts

Guest uploads use a signed browser-bound form and WordPress admin-post transport. The server reloads the matching shortcode from its stored page/post content before accepting a new request and before promoting processed media. Browser-submitted owner, gallery or hidden defaults never grant authority. Changed/removed forms, unreadable/password-protected content, stale grants and a different browser/login context stop processing. Guest forms must be declared in normal readable post/page content; dynamically injected widget/template/builder forms without a matching stored declaration fail safely and need a supported integration.

A successful or authorized failed POST redirects with HTTP 303 to a GET receipt. Reloading a receipt performs no image processing or publication. Each browser/form retains the same request identity across reloads and lost POST responses; an exact retry acknowledges its existing picture and changed bytes/metadata conflict. Check upload reads its state; Resume stored upload is a separate nonce-protected POST, always pending for unfinished guest work. Do not start another copy after uncertainty. If the original intake is missing, select the same picture and original field values; otherwise contact the administrator with the upload reference. Active workers, replaced temporary locks, changed files/roots and human-edited drafts require review. Recovery uses the same single-host safeguards as member journals.

Submit another picture is an explicit POST after completion or abandonment. An atomic private current-request pointer prevents an old tab from silently replacing a newer request. Guest upload cookies are site-specific, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax and Secure on HTTPS, expire after seven days, and contain only a random browser secret. Logged-in receipts additionally depend on that WordPress login session. Clearing cookies, switching browsers/logins or expiring the browser cookie loses self-service access; administrator journal inspection remains available. Exclude guest-form pages from full-page caches: the plugin sends private/no-store headers, and a cached grant from another browser is rejected.

Guest receipts reveal no picture/file URL, private picture ID, email, description or raw browser secret. Authorized validation failures preserve bounded text in one ten-minute feedback transient per browser/form, without file bytes, CAPTCHA tokens or nonces; expired stored transients may await WordPress cleanup. Successful feedback clears those text fields. The shared private upload journal retains source relationships, request fingerprints and submitted guest title/email/IP/metadata under the existing retention policy. Minimal current-request pointers, completion receipts and cleanup tombstones are retained to prevent duplicate replay; do not delete these records independently. Administrator recovery/abandonment/retention also supports owner ID 0 guest drafts. Deactivation/uninstall preserve this history and media.

Moderator notification is attempted at most once after the guest picture commits. An interrupted claimed delivery is not sent again automatically, so mail can be missed; Upload Journals shows its notification state for administrator review. No automatic retry sends duplicate mail. Legacy member AJAX/form/raw integrations use their own authenticated session-bound journal protocol, described below.

Frontend image tools and thumbnail sizes

Owners can use Edit image on their pictures or [videowhisper_picture_editor picture="123"]. [videowhisper_picture_manager] lists the current user’s pictures. The native editor is independent of membership content/monetization editing. Administrators can disable it in Display settings. Configured owner roles use a dedicated per-picture permission; other users require native object edit permissions. Guest-submitted records require a moderator. The tools open directly on the editor page. JPEG and PNG with a ready normalized media manifest are supported. Intact legacy pictures are prepared automatically when needed. Gallery listings, picture views/previews and dashboard lists/editors queue a background inventory; opening the frontend editor runs the same importer immediately. No files are regenerated or claimed by inventory. Existing images remain available while queued. Uncertain media still needs administrator Media Maintenance or repair. Unsupported, missing or ambiguous sources require repair before editing; GIF editing is unavailable.

Crop coordinates follow rotation and flips; resizing locks the aspect ratio without upscaling. Every save starts from the same normalized master. Users without native publishing capability and the configured publish policy send changes for review; existing public media stays unchanged. A moderator opens the same editor and approves its pending generation. Restore creates a fresh generation with the original composition and follows the same review rules. Original and master files are retained, as are recovery files. Crashed operations and orphan locks require administrator review rather than automatic takeover. The editor bounds processing memory/pixels, file history (200 owned files) and operation history (100 requests per picture); reaching a bound requires administrator review. No automatic pruning of edit history is enabled.

Thumbnails follow Display width/height without enlarging small sources. A listing queues up to three outdated pictures per request; WP-Cron generates replacements from the active image. Low-traffic sites or disabled WP-Cron can use Picture Gallery > Media Maintenance > Refresh next 5 thumbnails. The current page keeps its old thumbnail until a later refresh. Missing/unsupported sources remain preserved and reported. PhotoSwipe’s thumbnail strip is enabled by default; disable it in Display or use viewer_thumbs="0" on a shortcode. The viewer retains at most 21 nearby authorized items and shows 5–7 thumbnails around the selection; query scans are capped at 5,000 candidates. The image click opens the picture post; use the dedicated zoom button to zoom.

Cropper.js 2.1.0 is bundled locally under MIT with readable source and reproduction notes in scripts/cropper/readme.txt. No remote editor service or account is used. Public upload URLs remain public file storage, not protected downloads.

short_description: Responsive photo galleries, frontend image uploads and owner crop, resize, rotate and flip tools.
description:
Elevate your WordPress site with the Picture Gallery plugin, enabling users to easily upload and manage images through a frontend interface. This powerful plugin supports guest uploads with CAPTCHA, generates thumbnails, and integrates seamlessly into your WordPress Media Library. Whether you’re looking to display image portfolios or sell digital photos, this tool is equipped with AJAX updates for live listing, drag-and-drop uploads, and extensive customization options to meet all your photo gallery needs.

Benefits

  • Compact grid, metadata cards and legacy tiles with locally bundled PhotoSwipe.
  • Frontend image editing: crop, resize, rotate, flip, review and restore original composition.

  • Automatic queued thumbnail size refresh and an administrator batch tool.

  • Frontend & Backend Uploads: Allows both visitors and administrators to upload images conveniently.

  • Advanced Security Features: Includes optional Google reCAPTCHA v3 for spam checks; server-side permissions govern uploads.
  • Dynamic AJAX Photo Lists: Updates the gallery live without page reloads, enhancing user experience.
  • Comprehensive Integration: Adds pictures and thumbnails to the WordPress Media Library for easy management.
  • Customizable Access Controls: Set permissions for uploads and gallery views, ensuring content security.
  • Monetization Opportunities: Integrates with plugins like “MicroPayments/FansPaysite – Creator Subscriptions, Digital Content Monetization” to enable photo sales directly from your gallery.

Reliable member uploads

Member upload forms keep a request identity for each selected picture. Use Check / resume upload after an interrupted connection, or Retry same file to resend the same request. Reusing a request identity with changed image bytes or form fields returns a conflict. Successful uploads are distinguished from submissions awaiting review.

Unresolved browser receipts store the filename, request identity and form fields in session storage (up to 20 per form); successful receipts are removed. Member self-service recovery requires the same WordPress login session. Administrators can inspect the stored journal and recover it after that session expires, while keeping unfinished pictures pending for review. Private server journals retain request fingerprints and picture relationships to prevent duplicate imports; they are preserved on deactivation and uninstall. After eligible abandoned media is cleaned, a compact replay-blocking receipt remains without the original filename or form fields. Completed receipts do not block an administrator-authorized media purge.

Recovery supports a single processing host with working local file locks. Changes to that host, its temporary lock files or configured media storage require administrator review. Retrying a completed request never recreates a trashed or deleted picture. Guest forms use the browser-bound durable workflow described below. Legacy AJAX/raw integrations retain their compatibility responses and do not acquire the new request protocol automatically.

Administrator upload journals and abandoned media

Picture Gallery > Upload Journals lists at most ten records per page, with owner, processing state, picture relationship, worker availability and retention status. Inspect one journal before recovering or abandoning it. Recovery reuses the original picture, leaves existing completed publication unchanged, and sends unfinished drafts for review. Active editor locks, edited drafts, running workers, changed media, replaced temporary locks and different processing hosts require review; no forced takeover is offered.

Abandonment is an explicit, confirmed administrator action. It permanently removes only an unchanged unpublished upload draft; published and pending pictures are preserved. Media is retained indefinitely by default. Enabling cleanup for an abandoned request starts a fresh seven-day retention period, followed by a separate preview and apply step for at most five journals. Reinstating a hold stops future cleanup. No background deletion runs.

Cleanup requires unchanged files with creation evidence and no remaining references. Shared attachments, active/pending picture dependencies, unproven legacy staging files and ambiguous records are retained. Linked media holds cannot bypass the upload retention deadline. A cleaned request identity remains blocked permanently, including after a lost response, so retrying it cannot recreate deleted content. Files with incomplete creation evidence need manual review.

My Pictures and legacy uploads

Automatic page setup adds My Pictures alongside Pictures, Upload Pictures and Guest Picture. On existing sites it runs once when an administrator next visits wp-admin with automatic setup enabled; existing pages and content are preserved. The logged-in account menu places My Pictures immediately after Browse Pictures. Sites with automatic setup disabled can create a page containing [videowhisper_pictures author_id=”current”].

The shared list shows the current owner’s published, pending, draft, private and scheduled pictures with status labels, excluding trash. Anonymous visitors must log in. Use a numeric author_id to filter published pictures by author; omit it to browse all published pictures. Existing Paid Membership content-management edit links remain available. Picture-specific editing tools are planned separately. Listing requests are capped at 100 pictures and 1,001 pages, and use allowlisted sort keys. Missing thumbnails display a placeholder instead of starting processing during browsing. Exclude personalized shortcode pages from page/CDN caches; the plugin sends private/no-store headers.

Legacy member integrations can continue POSTing to vwpg_upload with the existing vwpg_upload_nonce security value and owner/gallery/category/tag/description fields (or X-Owner, X-Gallery, X-Category, X-Tag, X-Description raw headers). Accepted transports are file multipart, fileselect/fileselect[] forms (at most 20 files), and raw image bodies with X-Filename. All use the shared validator, EXIF processing, manifest and upload journal. HTML success/error responses and published-picture links are preserved; HTTP errors indicate failure. Tags and descriptions are preserved for multi-file forms too.

For retry safety, send a stable 20–80 character alphanumeric/underscore/hyphen request_id field or X-Request-Id header for one logical upload. Reusing it with changed bytes, filename or metadata returns HTTP 409. Multi-file array requests derive a separate identity as SHA-256(request_id + ‘:’ + array index), so retries must preserve file order. Omit the key only for older clients: each submission then creates a new journal and uncertain retries can still create another picture. Existing vwpg_upload_status POSTs use the same nonce and original request_id for single-file lookup/recovery. Recovery requires the same login session, processing host and original lock; administrator Upload Journals supports review. These member identities do not replace signed guest form grants.

Raw requests are streamed in bounded chunks to exclusive temporary files and cleaned on handled outcomes. An uncatchable worker termination before journaling can leave an unreferenced temporary file for host-level temporary-directory cleanup; the plugin never sweeps arbitrary temporary files. Shared-file checks scan at most 50,000 relevant metadata rows and 5,000 retention records in batches of 64, accepting at most 64 KiB per record. Matching option/content checks also use batches of 64 and a 64 KiB payload cap, with at most 1,000 candidate matches. Any scan overflow/error retains the file. Generic content/custom-field/option reference checks remain conservative and can retain false positives; the limits do not imply a complete indexed catalog or a large-site performance guarantee.

Administrator media diagnostics

Picture Gallery > Media Maintenance includes read-only diagnostics. Backend format flags are reported by the configured WordPress editor classes; they do not prove a complete decode/transform/save on this host. JPEG, PNG and GIF remain the upload allowlist. WebP/AVIF flags do not enable those formats or the planned frontend editor.

Effective image limits come from the same policy as image preflight: decoded pixels/edges, WordPress and raw-upload byte ceilings, and the current request’s conservative memory budget. Frontend requests can have different available memory; native library allocations are estimated. Storage checks only inspect whether the configured directory exists and appears writable, without creating it or establishing file ownership.

Counts describe at most twenty pictures and twenty upload records per cursor batch, not site-wide totals. Unknown/duplicate/oversized metadata is reported for review; unfinished uploads can be active or interrupted. Separate picture and upload cursors advance through later batches. No files, image jobs, manifests, locks or journal writes are created by diagnostics. Use the separate existing nonce-protected maintenance/recovery actions after inspection. Access requires administrator manage_options permission; submitted descriptions, email/IP, filenames, paths and worker credentials are excluded from the diagnostic summary.

Can I build a media reference index?

Administrators can use Media Maintenance to build the next 50 metadata and 20 journal/retention option records and prune the next 50 stale hints. The optional index is local to each site and is never created by browsing or activation. Verified hits can avoid broad scans; misses still use conservative scans. It does not establish file ownership, authorize deletion or remove any images.

How do I select grid, cards and PhotoSwipe?

In Picture Gallery settings, open Display and choose Responsive grid or Picture cards and the picture click action. Existing installations keep Legacy until you opt in; fresh defaults use grid and PhotoSwipe. Shortcodes can override these choices:

[videowhisper_pictures layout="grid" viewer="photoswipe" columns="3" perpage="12"]
[videowhisper_pictures layout="cards" viewer="photoswipe" author_id="current" show_caption="1"]

Modern galleries render images and pagination on the server, including without JavaScript. Search, tags, categories and date/view sorting enhance without replacing working images on errors. PhotoSwipe loads locally on first interaction, offers keyboard navigation/zoom/close and browses only the current authorized page. A separate picture details link remains available. Viewer failures preserve ordinary links. There is no periodic background gallery polling in these layouts.

The viewer checks access again when opened. Gallery role/free/registered/unpublished rules, object visibility, VideoWhisper membership roles, active micropayment purchases and paid-through author subscriptions apply before image serialization. Unknown paid states, WooCommerce and myCRED access fail closed unless a read-only entitlement integration confirms them. Public image URLs may still be directly accessible: this feature does not provide protected file storage. Physical files must be locally readable under approved upload/content roots. Very large or animated display images use an existing thumbnail; viewing never regenerates media. Frontend crop/resize/rotate/flip tools are included; masonry and justified layouts remain planned.

Bundled PhotoSwipe 5.4.4 is MIT licensed. Readable source, license and reproducible artifact instructions are included in scripts/photoswipe/readme.txt. No viewing assets are fetched from a CDN.

Existing pictures after an update

No full-library scan runs during activation or upgrade. Picture Gallery imports intact legacy media relationships on demand, preserving picture IDs, URLs, titles, authors, galleries, visibility and original files. Listings and views queue up to three new jobs per request; WP-Cron inventories at most three pictures per worker request without decoding images. Frontend image editing uses the same importer immediately, without waiting for cron. Dashboard lists and both classic/block edit screens also queue preparation automatically.

Ready records are reused. Each automatic inventory is limited to 64 MiB of distinct media files and uses the shared picture lock. Missing, changed, ambiguous, unsupported or unproven historical media stays preserved for review; no ownership is inferred from its location. Failed background imports pause for an hour unless legacy paths/size/mtime change. Opening the authorized frontend editor retries immediately. Disabled WP-Cron can delay background preparation; explicit Media Maintenance inventory remains available. Existing edit generations and unknown manifest versions are never replaced by automatic import.
